author: Youthful vigor

title: Not worth it!
body: I would highly recommend sticking with the book Atomic Habits rather than paying for this app. The app costs ¥1,500 per month, and I paid ¥18,000 for an annual subscription when it first came out. Now the annual fee has dropped to ¥10,000, and the only benefit I received was three extra months. The app’s functionality is pretty basic—you can only track a few things, and it doesn’t offer much more beyond that. On top of that, I have to log in every time I open the app, which is very frustrating. Overall, I’m extremely disappointed and feel it’s not worth the cost. I’m seriously considering asking for a refund.
author: eric412000

title: Good app ruined by greed
body: In no way is this app worth $16.99 a month. The free version only lets you set and track one habit. If you want to track more than one habit you have to buy the subscription. The paid version also has curated articles that are nice, but I’d recommend to save your money and just read Atomic Habits again. I’m big fan of James Clear so I was excited for this app, but honestly it seems like just a cash grab capitalizing on his fame in the productivity space. Pretty disappointing and changed my view of James.
author: Ledo392919

title: The rolling out of this app is as productive as the people behind it
body: I received the invitation to join the beta testing but it turned out that it had already reached the capacity. While I was thinking that this was going to be a long wait, just as many "productive" apps in beta out there which keep you on a waiting list for months or even years, the email I received 2 weeks later was the one that told me the official release was ready :)
